text:
Stop jobs going stale only because the post-landing rebuild (resync onto the merged commit) replaced the commit they were dispatched on. Outcome: (1) dispatch does not take the branch tip while a landing rebuild is in progress; it waits until the rebuild finishes. (2) In land.rs plan, when the job's base is not an ancestor of HEAD, look on the branch for a commit with the same tree as the base. If one is found, use it as the base and continue the normal checks (records-only replay, governed fingerprint). The job goes stale only if governed content really moved. (3) The stale-retry path in run/mod.rs (merging the kept candidate onto the tip) also accepts such an equivalent base, so it does not start from the beginning. Acceptance: a test dispatches a job, rebuilds the branch on a merged commit with an identical tree, and shows the job lands with no producer rerun. A second test shows a real governed change still makes the job stale. A third test shows dispatch during a rebuild waits. Add a CHANGELOG entry.

Acceptance:
- The change is made as described: Jobs dispatched while a landing rebuilds the branch go stale ('base no longer an ancestor') after passing, and their retry cannot reuse the kept candidate
- No unrelated behavior changes; the existing tests pass
- fmt, clippy and test pass

Files: land.rs, run/mod.rs
